newsitem.title: USA: IPO - CMP could catch small-caps' wind.
newsitem.headline: IPO - CMP could catch small-caps' wind.

text.p: Technology publisher CMP Media Inc, due to convert to a public company on Friday, could see its share price swept upward in a flury of smallcap optimism, an industry expert said.
"Market conditions for small-caps have never been better during the year," said Manish Shah, publisher of IPO Maven.
Initially valued at between $17.00 and $19.00 by underwriter Goldman Sachs, Shah predicted CMP would price at $19.50 and trade three to four points higher in opening trade.
"I think in the short-term, it will trade as high as 25," he added.
Shah cautioned, however, that the Internet had broken down barriers to entry in print publications, rendering competition more fierce and large publishers "less unique."
Also troublesome, analysts said, is a trend that shows computer advertising dollars flowing away from high-tech publications in search of a more general audience.

CMP's magazines and newspapers are geared toward the niche markets of computer electronics, information technology and the Internet, and the largest slice of its revenue comes from circulations funded almost exclusively by advertising.

"Generally the problem that this niche has is that computer-related subjects are becoming more and more mainstream," said Steve Mitra, senior analyst at Jupiter Communications. "It's not just the high-tech folks being targeted."
However, Mitra said CMP should be able to balance the steep competition among computer-oriented publications against expertise in its other niche markets.
"It's a good, strong publishing company, but not the leader in some of the hottest markets," said Richard Shaffer, principal of consulting company Technologic Partners.

Shaffer described CMP's Electronic Engineering Times magazine as "far and away the leader in its field" but said the company trailed behind International Data Group and Softbank Corp in producing an attractive PC publication.

Started in 1971 by Gerry and Lilo Leeds, who produced the first CMP publication in their living room, the company reported net income of more than $16 million in 1996, on revenues of $418 million. IPO Insider newsletter said in May while CMP tracked "less-than-staggering" revenue growth of 15 percent annually, net profit growth looked promising.
CMP saw its net income rise from $1.6 million in 1994 to $9.5 million in 1995 and $16 million in 1996.
